public.text: Regional governance is described mainly in relation to legal authority, sovereignty, and dispute resolution. It gives limited attention to differences in language, terminology editions, digital maturity, financing, infrastructure, and operational capacity across participating countries.
public.suggestedRevision: Expand regional considerations to include multilingual interoperability, maturity differences, shared-service funding, capacity support, service-level variation, cross-border incident response, and phased participation.
